system_description.narrative_title: A Fragile, Multipolar Order Strained by Markets, Energy Shock and AI Rivalry
system_description.narrative_summary: The global system is being pulled in three simultaneous directions: a volatile financial cycle driven by rising real yields and sovereign debt stress; an energy-security shock centered on the Iran war, Houthi attacks and disrupted shipping that is reordering suppliers and fuel politics; and an intensified strategic competition over AI, data infrastructure and cyber capabilities (China, US, EU and private tech capital). These dynamics interact with electoral politics (US midterms, European fiscal fights), kinetic and cyber attacks on critical infrastructure, and shifting defense alignments, producing feedback loops that amplify market, supply-chain and regional-security instability.
system_description.scope: Nation-states and alliances, major corporations and institutional investors, commodity (especially oil and gas) flows and logistics, sovereign and corporate debt markets, critical digital infrastructure (data centres, AI stacks, cyber operations), military and paramilitary actors, and international institutions and sanctions regimes.
system_description.super_system: The planetary socio-economic-security system: the integrated global order of politics, markets, technology and transnational networks within Earth's human ecosystem.
adjacent_subsystems: Climate and extreme-weather system (El Niño, hurricanes, supply disruptions)
Global public-health and biosecurity system (pandemics, laboratory incidents)
Transnational supply-chain and logistics network (shipping lanes, ports, tankers)

variables.name: Middle East maritime and energy conflict
variables.description: Iran and Iran-backed proxies, Saudi Arabia, the U.S. and other regional states are engaged in escalating maritime attacks and strikes that are disrupting oil flows, raising fuel prices and reshaping regional security dynamics.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine, with extensive Western military, economic and intelligence involvement, remain locked in a high-intensity war characterized by heavy strikes, territorial contestation and widening economic and strategic spillovers.

variables.name: US–China tech and trade rivalry
variables.description: The United States, China and their economic partners are competing intensely over AI, semiconductors, data governance and trade policies, producing export controls, investment shifts and industrial decoupling across global supply chains.

variables.name: Global bond and rate shock
variables.description: Surging U.S. Treasury and Eurozone yields, driven by tighter central-bank stances and fiscal stress (notably in parts of Europe), are reconfiguring capital flows, investor confidence and policy space across advanced economies.

variables.name: China–Taiwan gray-zone pressure
variables.description: China is intensifying military and political pressure on Taiwan through militia patrols, diplomatic coercion and other gray‑zone tactics, testing Taiwanese resilience and external deterrence commitments.
